question: What is the primary function of the ductus venosus in the fetal cardiovascular system?

options.A: Shunt blood from the umbilical vein past the liver
options.B: Drain deoxygenated blood directly back to the placenta
options.C: Direct blood from the right atrium to the left atrium
options.D: Connect the pulmonary artery to the descending aorta

explanation: The ductus venosus specifically connects the umbilical vein to the inferior vena cava, allowing well-oxygenated blood to bypass the hepatic capillary bed. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h1)

question: Why does the majority of fetal blood bypass the pulmonary circulation?

options.A: Fetal lungs are non-functional and filled with fluid
options.B: Systemic vascular resistance is lower than pulmonary resistance
options.C: The left ventricle pumps blood directly into the trachea
options.D: The placenta actively destroys pulmonary arterial blood flow

explanation: Because fetal lungs do not participate in gas exchange and are filled with fluid, pulmonary vascular resistance is very high, forcing blood through alternative shunts. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h1)

question: What primary physiological change occurs when the umbilical cord is clamped at birth?

options.B: Hepatic blood flow drops to absolute zero

explanation: Clamping the umbilical cord removes the low-resistance placental circuit, which immediately raises the systemic blood pressure and vascular resistance. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h2)

question: How does the first breath of a newborn directly affect the pulmonary blood vessels?

options.A: Alveolar pressure constricts the pulmonary capillaries
options.B: Cold air mechanically collapses the main pulmonary artery
options.C: Increased carbon dioxide triggers localized vasoconstriction

explanation: The influx of oxygen during the first breath serves as a powerful vasodilator, relaxing the pulmonary vasculature and allowing blood to flood the lungs. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h2)

question: What mechanical force causes the functional closure of the foramen ovale right after birth?

options.A: Increased pressure in the left atrium
options.B: Complete thrombosis of the interatrial septum
options.C: Decreased pressure in the right ventricle
options.D: Surgical ligation by the attending midwife

explanation: As pulmonary blood flow returns to the left atrium from the lungs, left-sided pressure exceeds right-sided pressure, physically sealing the flap valve of the foramen ovale. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h3)

question: Which chemical factor plays a major role in triggering the constriction of the ductus arteriosus?
explanation: The dramatic rise in blood oxygen levels after the first breath stimulates smooth muscle contraction in the wall of the ductus arteriosus. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h3)

question: Where does blood go immediately after leaving the right ventricle in a healthy newborn?

options.A: Directly back to the placenta via umbilical arteries
options.B: Through the ductus arteriosus to the aorta
options.C: Into the pulmonary arteries to the lungs
options.D: Across the foramen ovale into the left atrium

explanation: In established neonatal circulation, the right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood exclusively into the pulmonary circulation for gas exchange. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h4)

question: A newborn infant experiences severe birth asphyxia leading to prolonged hypoxia. Which complication is most likely to persist based on this physiological state?

options.A: Immediate closure of all systemic venous valves
options.B: Premature ossification of the ligamentum arteriosum
options.C: Rapid atrophy of the right ventricular muscle wall
options.D: High pulmonary vascular resistance keeping shunts open

explanation: Hypoxia causes sustained pulmonary vasoconstriction, preventing the normal drop in pulmonary resistance and often maintaining fetal shunting patterns like persistent pulmonary hypertension. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h4)

question: What is the hallmark physiological feature of Persistent Pulmonary Hypertension of the Newborn?

options.A: Spontaneous closure of the descending aorta
options.B: Excessive proliferation of umbilical vein tissue
options.C: Complete absence of the left ventricular chamber

explanation: PPHN occurs when pulmonary vessels fail to relax at birth, keeping pulmonary vascular resistance pathologically elevated. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical clinical consequence of right-to-left shunting through unclosed fetal pathways?

options.A: Differential cyanosis between upper and lower body
options.C: Perfusion of deoxygenated blood to the brain

explanation: Shunting deoxygenated blood past the lungs results in systemic hypoxemia and cyanosis throughout the body, rather than hyperoxygenation anywhere. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h5)
